summary: Deut 3:22 note: give the Leningrad Codex form with the tav's ḥiriq before its sheva, in plus notation and in a packed form whose CGJ (U+034F) holds that order, with prose calling it a reversed ḥataf-ḥiriq

Deuter.new: ל?!=תִּ+תְּירָא֑וּם (תִּ͏ְירָא֑וּם) בחטף-חיריק הפוך (!), דהיינו החיריק מימין לשווא,
Deuter.comment: Deuteronomy 3:22: the note's ל?! form of תיראום, whose tav the note says has a ḥataf-ḥiriq; give it with the ḥiriq before the sheva, in plus notation and in a packed form with a CGJ, and call it a reversed ḥataf-ḥiriq, the ḥiriq to the right of the sheva
